finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[CDN-1] Large media in public/ served from origin
File: public/wpvideo.mp4 (L1-L1)
Evidence: Repo contains multiple large static media in /public (mp4, webm, HEIC/JPG originals and many full-size images) which are referenced directly from pages (e.g., /bubu.jpg, /badge.jpg) and will be served by the app host if not fronted by a CDN. These files are not behind an image/video processing CDN in the repo and will be served at full size/quality.
Impact: High-traffic pages will egress large volumes directly from the origin, exhausting bandwidth and storage egress limits under concurrent users. 
Fix: Move large media to a purpose-built CDN/streaming service (Cloudflare Images/Stream, Cloudflare R2 behind CDN, or a separate CDN bucket) and update references to CDN URLs or use next/image with a CDN assetPrefix.

[CDN-2] Product APIs and storage listing not cacheable
File: src/app/api/products/[slug]/route.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: Product and storage-listing API routes return JSON with no Cache-Control / s-maxage / stale-while-revalidate headers (only a few routes set short private caches), so every client request will hit the origin/database. The product page fetches /api/products/[slug] server-side and the products list API is used client-side without CDN caching hints.
Impact: Under scale, dynamic but cacheable product reads will hammer origin CPU/DB and increase bandwidth — origin overload and poor cache hit ratio. 
Fix: Add cache headers (s-maxage + stale-while-revalidate) for product/listing endpoints or have the CDN cache these JSON responses; use ISR/edge caching for product pages.

[CDN-3] Videos served directly from storage without streaming/CDN
File: src/app/product/[slug]/page.tsx (L300-L380)
Evidence: Product page embeds video elements with <source src={video.videoUrl}> (videoUrl stored in DB/R2/public) and also ships large public video files; there is no evidence of adaptive streaming, range/byte request handling, or CDN/streaming service integration. Serving MP4/WebM directly will transfer full files on each view/seek.
Impact: Video playback will cause heavy egress and storage read IOPS, quickly exhausting bandwidth/egress quotas and causing slow page loads under concurrent viewers. 
Fix: Host videos behind a CDN/streaming service (Cloudflare Stream, signed URLs, or CDN-fronted R2) and enable range requests or adaptive streaming to reduce origin egress.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[CDN-4] R2 URLs bypass Cloudflare image variants (no resizing)
File: src/lib/cloudflare-images.ts (L1-L160)
Evidence: getCloudflareImageUrl/cloudflareImageLoader explicitly returns R2 URLs unchanged during migration ("If it's an R2 URL ... return imageUrl"), so images stored in R2 will not receive Cloudflare variant/resizing. 
Impact: Images served from R2 will often be full-size originals, increasing bandwidth and slowing pages compared to variant-resized Cloudflare Images.
Fix: Migrate images to Cloudflare Images variants or put an image-resizing CDN in front of R2; or generate/reserve resized variants on upload.

[CDN-5] Upload endpoint buffers large files in memory
File: src/app/api/admin/upload-image/route.ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: The upload route reads formData into a File -> arrayBuffer -> Buffer and allows files up to 100MB; uploads are proxied through the Node process before uploading to Cloudflare Images. 
Impact: Concurrent large uploads can exhaust server memory and CPU, leading to OOMs and slowdowns — a bottleneck under heavy admin usage or automated uploads.
Fix: Use direct-to-storage uploads (presigned URLs) or stream uploads to the storage provider to avoid buffering large files in the app process.

--- INFO ---

[CDN-6] next.config lists remote image domains and Cloudflare loader
File: next.config.ts (L1-L60)
Evidence: next.config.ts includes remotePatterns/domains for imagedelivery.net and R2 domains and comments about Vercel optimization and Cloudflare loader.
